_read_me: Every input for the Duke only traffic model. Nothing here comes from Birmingham or The Hague. Each item carries status: VERIFIED (read from the cited source), ASSUMPTION (our guess, change it freely), or PARTIAL. Lot coordinates are the named building next to each lot (from OpenStreetMap), not the lot outline.

d_factor.note: No NCDOT D factor for Research Dr; same 0.65 as the other campus roads

aadt_year_rule.why: NCDOT's 2025 layer adds 2023 and 2025 counts, which are past the 2021 pandemic dip. Science Dr and Towerview Rd still stop at 2017.

lots.name: Bryan Research Garage

lot_anchor_status.status: VERIFIED building coordinates from OpenStreetMap; the lot itself is next to the building, not at that exact point

road_weights_status.why: Equal split between the counted roads next to each lot.

street_hour_share.why: Share of a day's traffic in each hour (0 = midnight). No hourly counts exist for these roads that we could reach. Weekday has a morning and evening commute peak; weekends peak midday. Google Typical traffic showed every counted road green at every hour checked, so the peaks are not strong enough to jam.

day_factor.why: AADT is an average over all 7 days. Weekdays run above it, weekends below. 5 x 1.08 + 0.85 + 0.70 = 6.95, close to 7, so the week still averages to AADT.

lot_moves.why: Cars entering plus leaving each lot per hour = capacity x turnover x hourly share. Employee permit lots fill in the morning and empty late afternoon. Lots near classrooms get a small extra churn at Duke class change times.
lot_moves.class_change_hours_status: VERIFIED class start times; the size of the extra churn is ASSUMPTION
lot_moves.class_change_note: MWF starts 8:45, 10:20, 12:00, 1:40, 3:20, 4:55. TTh starts 8:30, 10:05, 11:45, 1:25, 3:05, 4:40. Counted in the hour the class starts.

calendar.staff_holidays_status: ASSUMPTION: Duke HR holiday page could not be read. Thanksgiving Day and the day after, Dec 24 to Jan 1, and MLK Day are treated as staff holidays.

no_class_lot_factor.why: Staff still work, students and some faculty do not.

no_class_campus_road_factor.why: Science Dr and Towerview Rd mostly serve campus.

events.status: VERIFIED dates and start times; the traffic boost and window length are ASSUMPTION

boost.why: Street traffic multiplier on affected roads during the event window.

events.window_status: Duke sets basketball checkpoints at Science/Cameron, Circuit/Towerview, Towerview/Duke University and Towerview/Science from 2 hours before tip-off until 45 minutes after the game (VERIFIED, https://parking.duke.edu/visitor-parking/athletic-event-parking/mens-basketball-parking/). 3 hours after start covers a roughly 2 hour game plus the exit (ASSUMPTION).

untimed.name: Women's basketball home game (time not read)
untimed.note: Dates VERIFIED by the research package; start times could not be read, so these days are flagged but not boosted.

google_typical_traffic.finding: Erwin Rd, Duke University Rd and NC 147 were green on Tuesday at 6:10, 7:00, 8:00, 8:55, 12:00, 15:50, 16:55, 17:55 and Saturday at 11:50 and 17:55. Science Dr, Towerview Rd (inside campus), Flowers Dr, Wannamaker Dr and campus Trent Dr have no traffic colour at all (Google shows no data for them).

direction.status: D factors VERIFIED where marked; which way the heavy flow goes, the hours it applies to, and the weights are ASSUMPTION
direction.why: NCDOT's D factor is the share of peak hour traffic going the busier way. It does not say which way. We assume the busy direction is toward campus in the morning peak and away from campus in the evening peak (Duke and the hospital are the main employers here), and an even split at other hours and on weekends.
direction.pattern_note: Share toward campus = 0.5 + (D - 0.5) x pattern. Pattern +1 = full morning peak, -1 = full evening peak, 0 = even split.

weight_away_from_campus.why: Leaving cars still crowd the road but cannot take a space.

direction.k_factor_check: NCDOT K factor (share of daily traffic in the design hour) on Erwin Rd is 0.085 to 0.100. The model's weekday peak hour is about 0.087 of daily traffic, inside that range.

measured_counts.status: VERIFIED when present: real counts from our own sensor. Until the file exists, no road uses it.
measured_counts.why: NCDOT has no count on Research Dr. The hardware team's magnetometer counts passing cars, which replaces a guessed hourly shape with a measured one.
measured_counts.format: Same CSV as park_shark.py reads: timestamp, sensor_id, group, kind, value. Only rows with kind = vehicle_count are used; value = cars since that sensor's last message.

min_minutes_per_hour.why: An hour only counts if its readings span at least this many minutes, so a half recorded hour is not mistaken for a quiet one.

counts_both_directions.why: We assume the magnetometer counts cars going both ways. Confirm with the hardware lead; if it counts one lane, double the counts or change the direction split.

measured_counts.how_used: For each date and hour: the exact measured count if one exists; otherwise the average measured count for that day type and hour, with the usual calendar and event factors; otherwise the road is skipped and the lot's other counted roads take its weight (same rule as before: weights split over counted roads).

reference_lot_rule.why: Index 100 stays tied to the original four lots (Trent Lot, 08:00 on a class Tuesday) so adding lots does not rescale old results. New lots have reference_lot = false.
